name: Just This Once
tagline: You don't get away with things. You get let off. That's better.
epigraph: The man sent to sell the gin in this glass said he never sold a bottle.
glassware: large wine glass (about 500 ml), filled with ice
language_row: Wren's 4-gram runs (the lint's own `ngrams()`) against every pour: clean in v2. Kept out: "line", "plain sight", "only if", "invitation", "ignored", "chosen" (siblings' words); no war, Prohibition, Jazz Age, "confidence man", parties, LAB or the 86 Company; never "Ford saved Plymouth". whoYouAre cut from 216 to 156 words. "he/his" only for Ford and Blacknell (lint warnings accepted by Wren, confirmed by Hester). ✓
sources: Studio fact card `_studio/fact-cards/simon-ford-plymouth.md`: *Oxford Companion to Spirits and Cocktails*, FORD, SIMON (pdf 828), FRENCH 75 (pdf 850–851), PLYMOUTH GIN (pdf 1538, 1541), PINK GIN (pdf 1520); Robert Simonson, *A Proper Drink*, pp. 108–112. Craft: *Cocktail Codex* pp. 138, 142. Audits: `work/regular-guy-outlaw/historian-audit-v1.md`, `-v2.md`. Room notes: `work/regular-guy-outlaw/`.
names_note: **Just This Once**, the room's pick (Hester and Tomás in the r5 vote; Wren took it in r5 step 2): what the guest says at the rule, and what the person behind the desk says back. *Hard to Dislike* was Wren's working title and vote, kept as the alternative for Robin. Also proposed: *Worth the Ask*, *Any Chance?*. Struck: *Go On, Then* (*Go On* is the Caring Leader's name), *Let Off* (near miss with the Saviour's room).
open_items: **Plymouth's 41.2% label ABV is unsourced** (no page we have gives today's label, and the web budget was spent). The recipe note covers it: a 44% gin takes 45 ml; the drink is swept at 40–44%.

**"Let off" is our word** (card C5): on the page it is "Ford stayed", "I didn't really mind", "I got funding to do more". That the dinners were public (press dinners) is our inference (C4); they're undated (C3), and no start year is given (C1).
**Ford is a living person:** every line about him is in the past tense. One web search (2026-10-01) showed no red flag; it's a search summary, not citable.

**The rule broken:** ice in Champagne, openly, in step 1. Oxford sides with it (the traditional French 75 is strained "into a highball glass filled with cracked ice"; the flute is Arnaud's, "counter to the original recipe", pdf 851). No Matrix spark: the ice is the one change. Balance: collins, 15.0% / 7.15 g / 0.95%, at the top of all three bands on purpose; in range through about 40 ml of melt.
**The plan's lead (Rowles) was replaced** by Wren in r1: he hides behind the union rule. Room chose Simon Ford.
